paper_metadata.title: Influence of composition and microstructure on the tribological property of SPS sintered MCrAlY alloys at elevated temperatures

evidence.quote: the present study aims to investigate the synthesis, microstructure, composition, mechanical and tribological properties of high-temperature monolithic MCrAlY (M=Ni or NiCo) alloys.

evidence.quote: Gas atomized prealloyed Ni-based alloy powders: NiCrAlY (commodity code is 962) and NiCoCrAlY (commodity code is 386-3) supplied by Sulzer Metco were used in this study.

The powder was weighed 200 g and sintered at 1150 °C in vacuum (<15 Pa) under a pressure of 30 MPa at a cylindrical graphite mold with a 50 mm diameter by spark plasma sintering technique, SPS (SPS-20T-10, Shanghai Chen Hua Technology Co., Ltd). The heating rate was 50 °C/min and the holding time 10 min. The sample was cooled down by circulating water in the intenders.

Compared with the microstructure of NiCrAlY, the particle of β-NiAl phase is refined (particle size is 5-8 µm in diameter), furthermore, the distribution of β-NiAl phase and Y is more uniform.

As for NiCoCrAlY, the main phases of sintered alloy are almost the same with raw powder. Compared with NiCrAlY, the main phases of NiCoCrAlY are β-NiAl and γ-Ni(Cr, Co) solid solution with small amount of γ'-Ni3Al reinforced phase.

According to the particle reinforcing principle of composite, particle reinforced composites are composed of larger size (> 1 µm) hard particles and matrix. Under the external load, the particles bear the load together with the matrix, obstruct the dislocation movement of the matrix and restrict the deformation of the substrate.
